name: Office core vocabulary
description: The 100 everyday workplace terms that anyone in any office role should know.

cards.subject: email
says: sends a written message electronically to one or more people
leaves a dated record that the sender and recipient can search later
cards.use: need to send a written message that the other person can answer when they are free
not: delivers only when both people are online at the same moment

cards.subject: bcc
says: copies a message to a person without the other recipients seeing their address
suits a mailing to many people who must not see each other's addresses
cards.use: email a long list of people who must not see each other's addresses
not: shows the copied person to everyone on the message

cards.subject: reply all
says: sends your answer to the sender and to every other recipient
can spread a private remark to people it was never meant for
cards.use: need everyone on a message to see your answer
not: sends your answer to the original sender alone

cards.subject: attachment
says: carries a file along with a message
can be refused or trimmed when it is too large for a mail system
cards.use: need to send a document together with your message
not: is typed into the body of the message as plain text

cards.subject: subject line
says: tells the reader what a message is about before they open it
helps people find the message again when they search
cards.use: want your email to be read quickly and found later
not: lists the people a message is copied to

cards.subject: out-of-office reply
says: answers senders automatically while you are away
tells people when you will be back and who to contact instead
cards.use: go on leave and want senders to know straight away
not: forwards every incoming message to your line manager

cards.subject: memo
says: records a decision, reminder or instruction for staff in a short formal note
is addressed within the organisation rather than to outside customers
cards.use: need a short formal note for staff that stays on record
not: is aimed mainly at customers outside the organisation

cards.subject: announcement
says: tells many people about a change or event at once
usually expects no reply because the information flows one way
cards.use: need to tell the whole team about a new starter or a change
not: is a private reply to one person

cards.subject: feedback
says: tells a person how their work or behaviour landed with others
works best when it is specific and about something they can change
cards.use: want a colleague to improve, or to keep doing something well
not: means praise only, with nothing to improve

cards.subject: follow-up
says: checks later that an agreed action was done
stops a conversation or request from being forgotten
cards.use: have heard nothing back about a request you made
not: is the first message in a new conversation

cards.subject: agenda
says: lists the topics a meeting will cover
is usually sent beforehand so people can prepare
cards.use: want a meeting to stay on track
not: records what was decided afterwards

cards.subject: taking minutes
says: writes down what was discussed and decided
gives people who missed the meeting an accurate account
cards.use: need a record of decisions for people who were not there
not: lists the topics before the meeting starts

cards.subject: action item
says: names one task and the person who will do it
comes out of a meeting as something to be done afterwards
cards.use: leave a meeting with a job you have agreed to do
not: lists everything that was discussed

cards.subject: attendee
says: is anyone who is invited to or present at a meeting
appears on the participant list of the meeting
cards.use: are counting who came to a meeting
not: is the minimum number of people needed for decisions to count

cards.subject: calendar invite
says: puts a meeting into each person's diary with its date, time and place or link
lets each recipient accept or decline
cards.use: need to book a time with several people
not: lists the topics to be discussed

cards.subject: stand-up
says: is a very short daily check-in where each person shares progress and blockers
is traditionally held on your feet to keep it brief
cards.use: want a quick daily sync with your team
not: is a long monthly planning workshop

cards.subject: one-to-one
says: is a private regular meeting between a person and their manager
covers workload, progress, worries and development
cards.use: need a private space to raise a worry or talk about growth
not: is a daily team check-in that everyone attends

cards.subject: briefing
says: gives people the facts they need before they act
is mainly one-way information from the person leading it
cards.use: need to bring a team up to speed before a task or event
not: is a private review of one person's performance

cards.subject: quorum
says: is the minimum number of members who must be present for decisions to be valid
leaves a meeting unable to make binding decisions when too few attend
cards.use: find too few members have turned up to make a binding decision
not: is the number of items on the agenda

cards.subject: any other business
says: is the final agenda item where extra topics can be raised
is often shortened to AOB
cards.use: have a small matter that is not on the agenda
not: is the first item, where the previous minutes are approved

cards.subject: project
says: is a piece of work with a goal, an end date and a team
ends when its goal is delivered rather than carrying on indefinitely
cards.use: have a one-off goal to deliver by a certain date
not: is routine work that repeats every day with no end

cards.subject: task
says: is one small piece of work given to someone
is normally finished by one person in a short time
cards.use: break a bigger job into pieces that people can pick up
not: marks an important checkpoint on the way to completion

cards.subject: milestone
says: marks a significant point reached on the way to completion
takes no time itself because it shows that something has been achieved
cards.use: want to show progress to a sponsor
not: is a single small job for one person

cards.subject: deadline
says: is the date or time something must be finished by
can be set by a law, a client or an internal plan
cards.use: need to know when work is due
not: is the plan that shows when everything happens

cards.subject: deliverable
says: is a thing a project promises to hand over, such as a report or a system
can be inspected and accepted by the person who asked for it
cards.use: need to say exactly what the client will receive
not: is a date marked on the plan

cards.subject: scope
says: sets out what a piece of work includes and what it leaves out
grows when extra requests are added without agreement
cards.use: get asked for extra work that is not in the agreement
not: is the order in which tasks are done

cards.subject: dependency
says: is something that must happen before another thing can start
delays a whole plan when it slips
cards.use: cannot start your task until someone else finishes theirs
not: is a task that can safely be skipped

cards.subject: priority
says: shows how urgent or important something is compared with other work
decides what to do first when time is short
cards.use: have more work than time
not: is the final date for finishing work

cards.subject: timeline
says: shows what happens when, in order
lays tasks and milestones against dates
cards.use: need to see the whole plan across time
not: lists only the people on the team

cards.subject: kickoff
says: is the first meeting that starts a project
makes sure the team shares the goal, roles and plan
cards.use: are launching a project with a new team
not: is the meeting that closes a project and reviews lessons

cards.subject: report
says: is a structured document that tells readers what happened or what was found
may include findings and recommendations
cards.use: need to give decision-makers the full picture
not: is a single number shown on a screen

cards.subject: summary
says: keeps only the main points of something longer
lets a busy reader grasp the essentials quickly
cards.use: have a long document and a reader with little time
not: adds detail that the original left out

cards.subject: dashboard
says: shows key numbers on one screen at a glance
often updates automatically from live data
cards.use: want to watch performance without opening a long document
not: is a written explanation with recommendations

cards.subject: metric
says: is a number used to measure one thing
only means something when compared with an earlier figure or a goal
cards.use: want to measure how something is going
not: is the goal a team is aiming for

cards.subject: KPI
says: is a metric chosen to show whether an important goal is being met
stands for key performance indicator
cards.use: need the few numbers that show if the organisation is on track
not: is any number that happens to be collected, whether or not it matters

cards.subject: target
says: is the number or result you are aiming for
gives a metric something to be compared against
cards.use: need to know what success looks like in numbers
not: is a prediction of what will happen

cards.subject: forecast
says: estimates what will happen later from current information
gets revised as new facts arrive
cards.use: need to predict next quarter's sales
not: states what you want to achieve

cards.subject: draft
says: is an early version that is not yet final
is shared so others can comment before it is finished
cards.use: want comments before you finish a document
not: is the agreed copy that replaces all others

cards.subject: final version
says: is the agreed copy that replaces all drafts
is the one people should use and store
cards.use: are about to send a document out
not: is an early copy that is still open to change

cards.subject: source
says: is where a fact or figure came from
lets a reader check whether a claim can be trusted
cards.use: need to show where a number came from
not: is a short version of a longer report

cards.subject: onboarding
says: helps a new person settle in and start work well
covers tools, introductions and first tasks over weeks or months
cards.use: have a new starter joining next week
not: is the process of ending someone's employment

cards.subject: induction
says: is the first formal introduction to an organisation and its rules
often covers safety, policies and who to ask for help
cards.use: need new people to learn the basics on day one
not: is the long process that lasts until a person is fully productive

cards.subject: probation
says: is an early trial period for a new employee
lets both sides decide whether the job is working
cards.use: are in the first months of a new job
not: is a reward for long service

cards.subject: line manager
says: is the person you report to day to day
usually approves your leave and runs your one-to-ones
cards.use: need to ask who approves your holiday
not: is the most senior person in the company

cards.subject: team lead
says: guides a team's daily work without necessarily being everyone's manager
often organises tasks and helps colleagues get unstuck
cards.use: need someone to coordinate the day-to-day tasks
not: decides pay and contracts for the team

cards.subject: colleague
says: is someone you work with
may be in your team or in a different department
cards.use: talk about the people you work alongside
not: is always someone who reports to you

cards.subject: job description
says: lists what a role does and what it requires
is a reference for what is expected of the post-holder
cards.use: need to know what a role is meant to do
not: records how well someone performed last year

cards.subject: appraisal
says: is a formal review of how someone is doing in their job
usually leads to agreed goals and a development plan
cards.use: reach the yearly time for a performance conversation
not: is the list of tasks that a role includes

cards.subject: handover
says: passes work and knowledge on to the next person
stops things being dropped when someone leaves or changes role
cards.use: are going on leave or moving to another team
not: is the first-day introduction for new staff

cards.subject: notice period
says: is how long someone must keep working after resigning or being dismissed
is normally set in the employment contract
cards.use: are leaving a job and need to know your last day
not: is a trial period at the start of employment

cards.subject: shift
says: is a set block of working hours
is common where a service runs beyond a normal day
cards.use: work early, late or night hours
not: is time off that the employer pays for

cards.subject: rota
says: is a schedule that shows who works when
is used where several people share the cover
cards.use: need to know when you are working next week
not: is a record of hours already worked

cards.subject: annual leave
says: is paid time off for holidays
is normally booked in advance and approved by a manager
cards.use: want to book a holiday
not: is time off taken only because of illness

cards.subject: sick leave
says: is time off taken because you are too ill to work
is reported to your manager rather than booked weeks ahead
cards.use: wake up too unwell to work
not: is booked weeks ahead as a holiday

cards.subject: flexitime
says: lets you choose start and finish times within agreed limits
often has core hours when everyone must be present
cards.use: want to start earlier so that you can finish earlier
not: pays a higher rate for hours beyond normal

cards.subject: hybrid working
says: splits time between an office and another place such as home
depends on which days a team agrees to be together
cards.use: work some days in the office and some at home
not: means working entirely from home

cards.subject: remote working
says: means working away from the office, usually from home
relies on online tools to stay in touch
cards.use: do your job from home with no office days
not: means splitting each week between the office and home

cards.subject: overtime
says: is work done beyond normal hours
may be paid at a higher rate or given back as time off, depending on the agreement
cards.use: are asked to stay late to finish something
not: lets you vary your start and finish times

cards.subject: timesheet
says: records the hours someone has worked
is often used to work out pay or to bill a client
cards.use: need to log the hours you have worked
not: shows who is scheduled to work next week

cards.subject: absence
says: is the general word for any time not at work, including unplanned time off
needs to be reported to your manager as early as possible
cards.use: cannot come in and must tell someone
not: is only counted when a person arrives late

cards.subject: invoice
says: is a bill a supplier sends asking to be paid
lists what was supplied, the amount and the payment date
cards.use: have done work and need to be paid
not: approves a purchase before it is made

cards.subject: purchase order
says: approves a purchase and its price before the goods or services are ordered
is sent to a supplier and later matched with their invoice
cards.use: need to authorise buying something from a supplier
not: is a bill asking for payment

cards.subject: budget
says: is the amount of money set aside for something
lets you compare what was planned with what is actually spent
cards.use: need to know how much you can spend
not: is proof that a payment was made

cards.subject: expense
says: is money you spend on work and claim back
normally needs a receipt before you are repaid
cards.use: pay for a train ticket that you will claim back
not: is the money a business earns from selling

cards.subject: receipt
says: is proof that a payment was made
is normally attached to an expense claim
cards.use: need to prove that you paid
not: is a bill sent before payment

cards.subject: quote
says: is a price offered before the work is agreed
can be accepted to turn into an order
cards.use: want to know the cost before committing
not: is a bill for work that is already done

cards.subject: payroll
says: is the process of paying employees
includes working out wages, tax and deductions
cards.use: need staff to be paid correctly each month
not: is the money paid to suppliers

cards.subject: cost
says: is what something takes to buy or do
is subtracted from revenue when working out profit
cards.use: need to know what something takes to provide
not: is the money a business earns from selling

cards.subject: revenue
says: is the money a business earns from selling, before costs are taken off
is sometimes called turnover or sales income
cards.use: need the total income from sales
not: is the money left after all costs are paid

cards.subject: approval
says: is official permission to go ahead
is often needed from a manager before spending or acting
cards.use: need a sign-off before a purchase
not: is proof that a payment has cleared

cards.subject: customer
says: is someone who buys from you
may buy once or many times
cards.use: talk about a person or business that pays for what you sell
not: is a business that sells goods to you

cards.subject: client
says: receives an ongoing professional service from you
usually has a relationship that continues for months or years
cards.use: work for an agency's long-term account
not: is only ever someone who buys once and is never heard from again

cards.subject: product
says: is something a business makes and sells
can be physical, like a device, or digital, like an app
cards.use: talk about what you sell as a thing
not: is work done for someone rather than an item

cards.subject: service
says: is work done for someone rather than a thing handed over
is delivered by people or systems over time
cards.use: sell consulting or repairs
not: is a physical item in a box

cards.subject: supplier
says: is a business that provides goods or services to you
is paid by you rather than paying you
cards.use: buy stock or materials
not: is a business that buys from you

cards.subject: vendor
says: is a seller, often of software or equipment
may be the company you subscribe to for a tool
cards.use: need to describe the company you buy software from
not: is a person who buys from you

cards.subject: contract
says: is a written agreement that both sides are bound by
sets out what each side must do and what happens if they do not
cards.use: need terms that both sides must follow
not: is a first offer that carries no obligation

cards.subject: proposal
says: offers a solution to a problem along with a price
is sent before a contract so the buyer can decide
cards.use: need to pitch your approach to a client
not: is legally binding the moment it is sent

cards.subject: complaint
says: states that something was not good enough
should be logged and answered within an agreed time
cards.use: hear a customer say they are unhappy with what they received
not: is a request for help using a product

cards.subject: support ticket
says: is a logged request for help that can be tracked until it is resolved
gives each problem a reference number
cards.use: need to report a fault so that it is not lost
not: is a formal statement that service was poor

cards.subject: spreadsheet
says: holds numbers and lists in a grid of rows and columns
can calculate totals automatically with formulas
cards.use: need to total a column of figures
not: stores a past version of every file you save

cards.subject: template
says: is a ready-made document that you copy and fill in
saves time and keeps documents consistent
cards.use: write the same type of document again and again
not: is a protected copy kept in case of loss

cards.subject: shared drive
says: is online storage that a whole team can open
keeps one copy that everyone works from
cards.use: want a team to find the same files in one place
not: holds only the files kept on your own laptop

cards.subject: access permission
says: decides who may view, edit or share a file or folder
can be set to read-only for some people
cards.use: need only certain people to be able to change a document
not: keeps a spare copy of the file

cards.subject: backup
says: is a spare copy kept in case the original is lost
should be stored separately from the original
cards.use: worry that a file might be deleted or a device might fail
not: shows who changed a file and when

cards.subject: version history
says: is the saved list of past changes to a file
lets you restore an earlier version
cards.use: need to undo an unwanted change that was made last week
not: is a copy stored on a different device

cards.subject: notification
says: is an alert that something needs your attention
can be turned off or limited to avoid distraction
cards.use: get a pop-up when someone replies to you
not: is a permanent record of a file's changes

cards.subject: user account
says: is your personal identity and access on a system
is protected by credentials that should not be shared
cards.use: need to sign in to a work system
not: is a shared login that the whole team uses

cards.subject: software licence
says: grants permission to use software under set terms
is often paid for per person or per device
cards.use: need to be legally allowed to use a paid program
not: is a spare copy of the software

cards.subject: helpdesk
says: is the team you ask when a tool or device is not working
logs your problem and works to fix it
cards.use: cannot log in or find that your laptop will not start
not: is the department that pays supplier bills

cards.subject: policy
says: is a rule the organisation has decided everyone follows
states what is expected without listing every step
cards.use: need to know what the organisation expects of you
not: lists the exact steps for one task

cards.subject: procedure
says: sets out the steps for carrying out a task the right way
helps different people do the same job consistently
cards.use: need to know how to do a task correctly
not: states a general rule without any steps

cards.subject: compliance
says: means following the laws, rules and standards that apply
is shown by evidence that the required steps were taken
cards.use: need to prove that the organisation follows the rules
not: is an independent check carried out once a year

cards.subject: confidential information
says: must not be shared beyond those who need it
includes things like salaries and client details
cards.use: come across a salary list or client details
not: may be passed freely to anyone who asks

cards.subject: data protection
says: is looking after personal information lawfully and safely
gives people rights over how their information is used
cards.use: handle customers' names and addresses
not: is keeping backups of all files

cards.subject: risk
says: is something that might go wrong, and how bad it would be
is rated by how likely it is and how serious its effect would be
cards.use: need to think about what could stop the plan
not: is something that has already gone wrong

cards.subject: audit
says: is an independent check that rules are being followed
produces findings and recommendations
cards.use: are being checked by an outside team
not: is the daily work of following the rules

cards.subject: incident
says: is something unplanned that harms or could harm work
is reported, recorded and reviewed
cards.use: see a system go down or someone get hurt
not: is something that might happen in future

cards.subject: escalation
says: passes a problem up to someone with more authority
is used when it cannot be solved at your level or in time
cards.use: cannot solve a customer problem yourself
not: means ignoring a problem until it goes away

cards.subject: health and safety
says: is keeping people from harm at work
includes reporting hazards and knowing where the fire exits are
cards.use: spot a wet floor or a trailing cable
not: is protecting the organisation's data

qa.q: Which part of an email tells the reader what it is about before they open it?
qa.right: The subject line
qa.why: The subject line is the short title shown in the inbox.

qa.q: A new colleague asks what a deadline is. What is the best answer?
qa.right: The date or time something must be finished by
wrong: A list of everything in a project
A meeting that starts a project
The person who approves the work
qa.why: A deadline is a time limit for finishing work.

qa.q: What is the main job of an agenda?
qa.right: To list the topics a meeting will cover
wrong: To record what was decided afterwards
qa.why: An agenda sets out the topics beforehand; minutes record what happened.

qa.q: Who is your line manager?
qa.right: The person you report to day to day
wrong: Anyone who works in the same room
The colleague who sits next to you
qa.why: A line manager is the person you report to directly.

qa.q: Which document is a bill that a supplier sends asking to be paid?
qa.right: An invoice
qa.why: An invoice asks for payment; a purchase order approves a purchase.

qa.q: Which pair is correct?
qa.right: A laptop is a product; repairing it is a service
wrong: A laptop is a service; repairing it is a product
qa.why: A product is a thing handed over; a service is work done for someone.

qa.q: Your laptop will not start and you have a meeting in ten minutes. Who do you contact first?
qa.right: The helpdesk
qa.why: The helpdesk logs and fixes problems with tools and devices.

qa.q: You notice a trailing cable across a corridor. What should you do?
qa.right: Report it, and make it safe if you can do so without risk
wrong: Leave it because someone else will notice
qa.why: Reporting hazards is a basic part of health and safety.

qa.q: You want comments on a document before it is finished. What do you send?
qa.right: A draft
qa.why: A draft is an early version shared for comment.

qa.q: You are emailing 200 customers about a change and they must not see each other's addresses. Where do you put them?
qa.right: In the bcc field
qa.why: Bcc hides the recipients from one another.

qa.q: Someone sent a private remark to a 300-person email by mistake. What was the likely error?
qa.right: Using reply all instead of replying to the sender
wrong: Sending an attachment that was too large
qa.why: Reply all goes to everyone on the original message.

qa.q: A meeting ends with the words 'Priya will send the figures by Friday'. What is that?
qa.right: An action item
qa.why: An action item names one task and who will do it.

qa.q: What is the difference between a milestone and a task?
qa.right: A milestone marks a point reached, while a task is a piece of work to be done
wrong: A milestone is small and a task is big
A milestone is always a meeting and a task is a report
qa.why: A milestone shows achievement; a task takes effort.

qa.q: A client asks for extra reports that are not in the agreement. What is the right response?
qa.right: Say it is outside the agreed scope and agree time and cost before doing it
wrong: Do it quietly and say nothing
Add it under any other business
qa.why: Extra work outside scope should be agreed, not absorbed.

qa.q: Which of these is best described as a KPI?
qa.right: Customer complaints answered within two working days, tracked against a goal
wrong: A list of every email received
The booking of a meeting room
qa.why: A KPI is a metric chosen to show progress towards an important goal.

qa.q: A director has two minutes to understand a 40-page report. What do you give them?
qa.right: A one-page summary
qa.why: A summary keeps the main points for a busy reader.

qa.q: A colleague leaves tomorrow and has several tasks in progress. What should happen?
qa.right: They write a handover for the person taking over
wrong: They delete the files so nobody gets confused
They send an announcement saying they are leaving
qa.why: A handover passes on work and knowledge.

qa.q: When is a purchase order normally raised?
qa.right: Before ordering, to approve the purchase
wrong: After delivery, to ask for payment
Only at the end of the year
qa.why: A purchase order approves a purchase in advance.

qa.q: You paid for a taxi on a client visit. What do you need to claim the money back?
qa.right: A receipt submitted with an expense claim
wrong: A purchase order from the taxi firm
qa.why: Expenses are normally reclaimed with a receipt.

qa.q: A customer asks how to reset their password. How should you log it?
qa.right: As a support ticket
qa.why: A request for help is a support ticket, not a complaint.

qa.q: A document gives the exact steps for processing a refund. What is it?
qa.right: A procedure
qa.why: A procedure sets out steps; a policy states a general rule.

qa.q: Sam works 7 to 3 on Monday instead of 9 to 5, with the same total hours. What is this?
qa.right: Flexitime
qa.why: Flexitime lets people shift hours within agreed limits.

qa.q: A new employee is told that their first six months are a trial. What is this called?
qa.right: Probation
qa.why: Probation is an early trial period.

qa.q: A freelancer sends a document offering a solution and a price for the client to consider. What is it?
qa.right: A proposal
qa.why: A proposal offers a solution and price before anything is agreed.

qa.q: Two people edit different copies called report_v2 and report_final2. What prevents this?
qa.right: One shared copy with version history
qa.why: A single shared file with version history avoids conflicting copies.

qa.q: A chart says sales rose 40 per cent but does not say where the figure came from. What should a careful reader ask?
qa.right: What is the source?
qa.why: Without a source, the claim cannot be checked.

qa.q: A colleague asks you to tell them another employee's salary and says it is fine. What do you do?
qa.right: Decline, because it is confidential and they may not need it
wrong: Tell them, since they asked politely
Post it on the shared drive
qa.why: Salaries are confidential information.

qa.q: The company installs paid design software on 30 laptops but bought 20 licences. What is the issue?
qa.right: It may break the licence terms
qa.why: A software licence limits how many can use the software.

qa.q: You ask three suppliers for a price before choosing one. What do you ask them for?
qa.right: A quote
qa.why: A quote is a price offered before the work is agreed.

qa.q: Design cannot start until the budget is approved. What is the approval?
qa.right: A dependency
qa.why: Design depends on approval happening first.

qa.q: You overwrote a file an hour ago and want the old text back. Where do you look first?
qa.right: The file's version history
qa.why: Version history lets you restore earlier versions.

qa.q: What is the difference between a target and a forecast?
qa.right: A target is what you aim for; a forecast is what you expect to happen
wrong: A target is a prediction; a forecast is a goal
A target is always lower than a forecast
qa.why: A target is a goal and a forecast is an estimate.

qa.q: What is the difference between induction and onboarding?
qa.right: Induction is the first formal introduction; onboarding runs longer until the person is settled
wrong: Onboarding is the first day only; induction lasts a year
qa.why: Onboarding is the longer process; induction is the start of it.

qa.q: A committee needs five of its nine members to vote. Only four turn up. What can it do?
qa.right: Discuss, but not make binding decisions
wrong: Vote anyway and record the result as final
Count the chair as two members
qa.why: Without a quorum, decisions are not valid.

qa.q: A customer's issue is past the promised response time and you cannot fix it. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Escalate it to someone with the authority to resolve it, with the details
wrong: Wait for the customer to give up
Send it to everyone with reply all
qa.why: Escalation passes the problem up when you cannot solve it.

qa.q: An outside team samples your records to see whether the correct procedures were followed. What is this?
qa.right: An audit
qa.why: An audit is an independent check that rules are followed.

qa.q: Which of these is an incident rather than a risk?
qa.right: The booking system crashed at 9am
wrong: The booking system might crash if demand doubles
A supplier may raise prices next year
A new rule may change our process
qa.why: An incident has already happened; a risk is something that might.

qa.q: Midway through a project, the sponsor adds a new feature with no extra time or money. What is the best response?
qa.right: Raise it as a scope change and agree time, cost or what to drop
qa.why: Scope changes should be agreed openly.

qa.q: Task B depends on Task A, which is two weeks late. What is likely to happen to Task B?
qa.right: It cannot start on time, so the plan is likely to slip
qa.why: A late dependency delays the work that relies on it.

qa.q: A dashboard shows 40 numbers, but leaders look at five linked to the organisation's goals. What are the five?
qa.right: KPIs
qa.why: KPIs are the metrics that show progress against key goals.

qa.q: Alex leaves on Friday and nobody knows where the supplier contract is stored. What should have prevented this?
qa.right: A proper handover
qa.why: A handover passes on knowledge such as where files are.

qa.q: A laptop is stolen. Which protects the files that were on it?
qa.right: A backup stored somewhere else
wrong: Version history kept on the same laptop
qa.why: A backup must be separate from the original.

qa.q: A manager asks you to place a £5,000 order, but anything above £1,000 needs sign-off. What do you do first?
qa.right: Get the required approval and raise a purchase order
wrong: Place the order and ask later
Split it into five smaller orders
qa.why: Approval comes before purchasing, and splitting orders avoids the control.

qa.q: An angry customer emails a complaint. What do you do first?
qa.right: Log it, acknowledge it and say when they will get a full answer
wrong: Mark it as a support ticket and close it
qa.why: A complaint should be logged and acknowledged with a time for a full reply.

qa.q: You are away for two weeks. What should your out-of-office reply include?
qa.right: The dates you are away and who to contact instead
wrong: Your password so that someone can cover
A list of all your open tasks
qa.why: Senders need dates and an alternative contact, not private details.

qa.q: Two attendees remember a decision differently. What settles it?
qa.right: The approved minutes, corrected if they are wrong
qa.why: Approved minutes are the agreed record of what was decided.

qa.q: A leaver still has access to the shared drive two months later. What was neglected?
qa.right: Removing their user account and access permissions when they left
qa.why: Access should be removed when someone leaves.

qa.q: A forecast made in January differs from actual figures in June. What is sensible?
qa.right: Revise the forecast using the new information
wrong: Change the actual figures to match
Delete the forecast and not replace it
qa.why: Forecasts are estimates and should be updated.

qa.q: A newsletter went out with every customer's address visible in the 'to' field. What is the risk?
qa.right: A data protection breach because personal addresses were exposed
qa.why: Exposing personal data to others can be a data protection breach.

qa.q: A printout of customer names and addresses is found in a shared kitchen. What should you do?
qa.right: Secure it and report it as a possible data protection incident
wrong: Pin it up to find the owner
qa.why: Personal data left out should be secured and reported.

qa.q: Staff are regularly asked to work late with no agreed extra pay or time back. What should clarify this?
qa.right: The overtime terms in the contract or policy
qa.why: Overtime arrangements should be set in the contract or policy.
